rag.name: DeltaSumCircuitsAux
rag.content:
/-- Circuits in `M₁ Δ M₂` are nonempty subsets of the ground set of form `X₁ Δ X₂`
    where `X₁` and `X₂` are disjoint unions of circuits in `M₁` and `M₂` respectively. -/
def DeltaSumCircuitsAux [DecidableEq α] (M₁ M₂ : BinaryMatroid α) (C X₁ X₂ : Set α) : Prop :=

rag.name: Matroid.DisjointCircuitFamily.union_subset_ground
rag.content:
/-- Union of sets in `M.DisjointCircuitFamily` is subset of ground set. -/
lemma Matroid.DisjointCircuitFamily.union_subset_ground {M : Matroid α} (F : M.DisjointCircuitFamily) :
    F.union ⊆ M.E := by
  simp only [Matroid.DisjointCircuitFamily.union, Set.iUnion_coe_set, Set.iUnion_subset_iff]
  exact fun i hi => mem_subset_ground F ⟨i, hi⟩

rag.name: Matroid.IsUnionDisjointCircuits.subset_ground
rag.content:
/-- Union of disjoint circuits is subset of ground set. -/
lemma Matroid.IsUnionDisjointCircuits.subset_ground {M : Matroid α} {X : Set α} (hMX : M.IsUnionDisjointCircuits X) :
    X ⊆ M.E :=
  have ⟨F, hXF⟩ := hMX
  hXF ▸ F.union_subset_ground

lemma Matroid.Circuit.subset_ground (M : Matroid α) {C : Set α} (hC : M.Circuit C) : C ⊆ M.E :=
  hC.left.right

    F.F x ⊆ M.E :=

variable {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] {C : Set α} {p : α}

set_option linter.unusedVariables false
informal_statement: For any two binary matroids \( M₁ \) and \( M₂ \), and for any cut \( C \) and element \( p \), if \( C \) is a circuit in \( M₁ \), then the singleton set containing \( p \), denoted \( \{p\} \), is a subset of the ground set \( M₁.E \).
informal_proof:
We begin by considering an arbitrary cut \( C \) in \( M₁ \) and an element \( p \). Since \( C \) is a circuit in \( M₁ \), we know that it satisfies certain properties inherent to matroid theory, particularly concerning its relationship to the ground set \( M₁.E \).

To show that \( \{p\} \subseteq M₁.E \), we utilize the lemma `Set.union_subset_iff`, which provides a method to derive subset relationships involving unions of sets. Specifically, we apply this lemma to derive the implication that if the union of two sets is a subset of another set, then each individual set must also be a subset of that set.

Given that \( C \) is a circuit and \( p \) is an element associated with \( C \), we deduce that \( \{p\} \) must indeed be a subset of \( M₁.E \). This follows logically because \( p \) is part of the structure defined by \( C \), and therefore, it must belong to the ground set of \( M₁ \).

Thus, the proof concludes that \( \{p\} \subseteq M₁.E \) holds true under the given conditions.

C1_dependencies.content:
@[simp]
theorem union_subset_iff {s t u : Set α} : s ∪ t ⊆ u ↔ s ⊆ u ∧ t ⊆ u :=
  (forall_congr' fun _ => or_imp).trans forall_and
